subject: English 1st Paper

source.edition: Revised for the year 2026; revised edition October 2025

passagePolicy: Use the specifically cited source section in the NCTB textbook. Full textbook passages and images are not reproduced. Original writing models are not source facts.

activities.instruction: Answer using the cited text. Equivalent accurate wording is acceptable; support interpretations with details.

items.question: What are the classmates planning?
items.modelAnswer: They are planning how to spend a week’s vacation.

items.question: What does the Kuakata advertisement attract Bahar’s attention to?
items.modelAnswer: It attracts attention to a two-day trip, the beach and sunrise.

items.question: Where does Azim suggest going, and why?
items.modelAnswer: He suggests the Chimbuk Mountains in Bandarban because he has wanted to climb a mountain.

items.question: Why does Shujan suggest the Sunderbans?
items.modelAnswer: He wants to see wild animals and take pictures of the forests and the sea.

items.question: Have they chosen a final destination at the end of the dialogue?
items.modelAnswer: No. They agree to consider the options before deciding.

activities.instruction: Explain the word in the cited context, or give the requested alternative meaning. Accept suitable equivalent wording.

acceptedAnswers: a period away from usual school or work
very attractive or impressive in this dialogue

activities.instruction: Write a short conversation choosing a class project together.

modelAnswer.speaker: Mina
modelAnswer.text: What should we make for our class project?

modelAnswer.speaker: Rafi
modelAnswer.text: How about a poster on keeping the school clean?

modelAnswer.speaker: Mina
modelAnswer.text: That sounds useful. We could include drawings and short instructions.

modelAnswer.speaker: Rafi
modelAnswer.text: Let’s ask our group members for their ideas before deciding.

modelAnswer.speaker: Mina
modelAnswer.text: Good idea. Then we can agree on the work together.

activities.note: Original classroom dialogue; not a continuation of the holiday discussion.
assessment: Addresses the task with relevant details
Uses a clear sequence and connected sentences
Uses suitable vocabulary and comprehensible grammar
Accept original accurate responses; do not require memorisation
